risks.risk: Exact keyboard model/specs (number of keys, power type, built-in sounds, connectivity) are not readable, so the price could be wrong for the actual item.
risks.proof: Ask for a clear photo of the keyboard control panel/spec label (underside/back) showing model number and power requirements.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a generic mini/educational keyboard with unknown functionality.

risks.risk: Functionality is unknown (keys may be stuck, missing, or not producing sound). Photos only show appearance.
risks.proof: Ask for a short video: power on + play a few keys + show volume/sound output.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not guaranteed working (worst case).

risks.risk: Accessories/charger/cables may be missing (common for keyboards). Photos do not show what comes with it.
risks.proof: Ask for a photo of everything included laid out (charger/battery compartment cover/manual).

risks.risk: Case condition and fit may affect usability (hinges/latches could be damaged). Photos show the case but not latch/hinge condition clearly.
risks.proof: Ask for close-up photos of the latches/hinges and a shot showing the keyboard seated properly in the case.
risks.if_unproven: Price assuming average wear and possible minor case issues.

proof_requests: Send a clear photo of the keyboard’s label/underside showing model number and power type (battery/adapter).
Send a short working video: power on, press several keys, and show sound output.
Show what’s included: charger/adapter (if any), battery cover, and any manual.
Close-up photos of the case latches/hinges and a shot of the keyboard fully seated in the case.
response.reason: The photos confirm it’s a portable mini keyboard in a case, but the model/specs and working condition are not verifiable remotely, so a safe price can’t be set without proof.
